note.summary: This chunk explains how to make a Temporary Repatriation Facility (TRF) designation for pre-6 April 2025 foreign income and gains, including identifying qualifying overseas capital, completing boxes 50-54 on SA109, currency conversion rules, calculation of the flat 12% TRF charge, and record-keeping obligations. It then transitions into the separate HS264 Remittance Basis 2025 helpsheet, covering who can claim the remittance basis, the deemed domicile rules, what counts as a remittance, the definition of 'relevant person', and business investment relief.

note.summary: HS264 explains the abolition of the remittance basis from 6 April 2025 and the transition to arising-basis taxation for UK residents, with the FIG regime available to 'qualifying new residents'. It covers how pre-6 April 2025 unremitted foreign income and gains are taxed if later remitted, unless designated under the temporary repatriation facility (TRF), and gives guidance on completing the Foreign pages (SA106) and Residence and FIG regime pages (SA109). It defines 'remitted to the UK', 'relevant person', and 'mixed fund', and explains business investment relief and foreign tax credit relief for remitted income.

note.summary: This chunk explains how mixed funds (containing multiple income/capital types or years) are treated under statutory ordering rules for remittance basis purposes, and directs readers to RDR1 for pre-2017 treatment while noting mixed fund cleansing was only available 6 April 2017 to 5 April 2019. It gives detailed instructions for completing the 'Foreign' pages boxes 1, 2 and 7.3-7.5, covering unremittable income, Foreign Tax Credit Relief (with worked examples), Special Withholding Tax treatment and set-off timing, foreign dividend taxation at normal rates rather than dividend rates, foreign pensions post-6 April 2017, and apportionment of foreign tax on partly-remitted overseas property income.
